scope: Proposition 3.4 (Uniform confinement of all rays) of the manuscript “No bigeodesics in planar first-passage percolation” (preprints/No-bigeodesics-in-planar-first-passage-percolation-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 212 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f97d87dc82bcee0c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 11. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Almost surely there is a finite H(z) ≥ 1 for every z ∈ Z2 such that every upper ray from z lies in Q+(z, H(z)) and every lower ray from z lies in Q−(z, H(z)). Moreover, for every fixed L < ∞, (12) max |z|≤Ln H(z) = o(n) (n → ∞). These statements hold simultaneously for every ray in the chart; no uniform rate of Busemann convergence over the intermediate labels is required.
